A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original formal-language meta-learning experiments, including transfer comparisons, LSTM–GRU comparisons, and length-generalization results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results, updates reported scores, and adds evaluations using alternative continuation metrics.

M1.justification: The first-order MAML procedure, recurrent architectures, vocabulary permutation, and downstream SGD/Adam training remain unchanged. Expanded explanations do not establish a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the 5000-grammar collection and the same nine formal languages spanning three Chomsky-hierarchy levels. The new grammar examples illustrate existing coverage; no additional task or domain is evaluated.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged: simplicity/complexity sampling conditions, mechanistic-complexity conditions, models without meta-training, and the LSTM–GRU comparison. Newly discussed prior work is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Figures 9–10 add evaluations replacing the better-than component of continuation F1 with BC, WORST, or POSSIBLE with alpha = 0.5. The original evaluation corpus, training-set sizes, principal metric, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused metric-sensitivity analysis testing whether Figure 2's conclusions survive alternative recall-like measures. The original architecture comparison and length-generalization analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2's Figure 2 caption newly specifies averaging over three meta-learning runs. v1 provides no corresponding run count, so this establishes additional reporting rather than an explicit increase in runs. Neither version explains the statistical meaning of the shaded bands.

E6.justification: Figures 2–6 revise quantitative evidence across aggregate comparisons, language-pair transfer, architecture comparisons, and length generalization. For example, Figure 3's context-free-to-context-free cell with ten training strings changes from 0.63 to 0.58. Figure 10 adds alternative-metric results, including the WORST exception. These are extensive result updates, although the principal qualitative conclusions persist.

T1.justification: Figure 9 adds mathematical definitions for alternative continuation measures, including the scaled minimum probability WORST and threshold-based POSSIBLE. The original continuation-F1 definition is retained; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions remain unchanged, but Section 6 shifts from saying MAML does not bestow a simplicity bias to saying it does not bestow a specific prior. New Section 2.1 frames the disputed claim as recovery of the intended prior while accepting a Bayesian parameter-prior interpretation.

C2.justification: Section 2.1 adds a substantive distinction between an architecture-dependent learned prior and the intended task-distribution prior. Figure 9 explains the WORST exception through sensitivity to the least likely valid token. The explicit limitations, including the absence of direct hidden-state evidence for counters, are unchanged.

D1.justification: Figures 7–8 newly document the grammar MDL calculation, its seven possible lemmas and five feature types, and concrete grammar examples. These improve reproducibility information without establishing a changed calculation. Appendix A's hyperparameters, software, and compute disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands substantially through Section 2.1's engagement with Grant et al. (2018), additional foundations for simplicity and MDL, and discussion connecting the proposal to Transformer expressivity and structured pretraining. These additions broaden and qualify the relationship to prior research beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 inserts Section 2.1, expands the motivation for the experimental predictions, and edits discussion passages and captions. Most prose and the overall section sequence are retained, so the narrative revision is limited.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial appendix displays for MDL, example grammars, metric definitions, and alternative-metric results. It also substantially enlarges Figure 5, revises several plot labels and legends, and reverses the order of the language-description and length-definition tables.

improvement.justification: v2 improves interpretive precision through Section 2.1, makes grammar construction more reproducible, discloses three-run averaging, and tests metric sensitivity while reporting the WORST exception. These are useful, evidence-supported gains. They remain limited because the underlying experimental scope is unchanged and the acknowledged absence of direct evidence identifying the proposed neural counters remains unresolved.
